left.description: This mezmur is a heartfelt plea to the Virgin Mary for comfort and help during times of sorrow and distress. It expresses deep personal pain, loneliness, and spiritual struggle, while seeking refuge in her compassion. The chant portrays the believer as broken and hopeless in the eyes of the world, yet still holding onto faith through her intercession. It emphasizes her role as a source of consolation, guidance, and protection, asking her to strengthen faith, prevent spiritual downfall, and restore peace. Ultimately, it reflects trust in her mercy as a loving mother who supports her children in their weakest moments.

It calls believers to walk steadfastly in faith toward this eternal home.

IN THE LAND OF EPHRATAH, IN BETHLEHEM’S CITY (×2),
THE SAVIOR HAS BEEN BORN, FROM  SAINT VIRGIN MARY, (×2)
THE LUMINOUS STAR CAME, DESCENDING FROM THE SKY (×2)
ALL CREATURES PRAISED THE LORD, “HALLELUJAH” THEY SANG /CRIED.
HALLELUJAH” THEY CRIED.

AS THE SHEPHERDS HERDED THEIR FLOCKS DURING THE NIGHT,
THEY HEARD THE GOOD TIDINGS DESCENDING FROM THE HEIGHT
THE ANGEL’S GLORY SHONE, BLAZING THROUGHOUT THE LAND,
A SIGHT THAT SHOOK THEIR HEARTS, TOO TREMBLING TO WITHSTAND.

HEAVEN’S HOSTS OF ANGELS APPEARED IN SUDDEN LIGHT,
IN ONE ACCORD THEY SANG WITH THE SHEPHERDS THAT NIGHT;
GLORY BE TO THE LORD IN THE HIGHEST HEAVEN,
AND PEACE UNTO MANKIND, TO THOSE IN HIS FAVOR.

TO BETHLEHEM THEY WENT, THEY HAILED THE NEWBORN LORD
IN THE MANGER HE'S FOUND, WITHIN HIS MOTHER’S HOLD
THE SHEPHERDS SPREAD THE WORD—THE ANGELS’ SONG THEY’D HEARD;
WITH THEIR HEARTS FULL OF PRAISE, THEY GLORIFIED THEIR GOD.

GOOD NEWS OF JOY FOR ALL, THE PEOPLE OF THE LORD;
IN DAVID’S HOLY TOWN, THE SAVIOR HAS BEEN BORN.
THEY LOOKED IN THE MANGER, THE CHILD WITH HIS MOTHER;
FOR HE IS THE SIGN OF SALVATION OF THE WORLD.

ሰምተን ስላደግን ከገድላት አንደበት
መስዋዕትም ቀርቧል ከፊታችን

አልጠፋችምና በእሳት ተፈትና

right.description: This mezmur is a hymn of veneration to the Virgin Mary, greeting her with titles drawn from the Old Testament and sacred tradition. She is symbolically identified with holy objects and events such as Noah’s Ark, Aaron’s rod, Gideon’s fleece, Jacob’s ladder, and the manna of heaven—each pointing to her role in bearing Christ. The chant emphasizes her purity, divine selection, and her place as the Mother of God (Eme Egziabher). Through poetic praise, the faithful honor her as the fulfillment of biblical types and approach her with reverence, asking for her blessings and intercession.
